top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock is an original invention with a named originator (Katori's magic-wavelength lattice), taken to the 10^-18 regime by Ye's group, and verified by independent clock-to-clock comparisons at several laboratories. It is a new principle and a tool that opens a door, not a better version of the 2005 or 2012 work. The citation should name the invention and leave out the redefinition of the second. Omitted contributors are a known risk but do not outweigh a clear original-work record, so I prefer it to no award.
